cards.text: John, God's servant (Revelation 1:1), has been watching the Lamb, Jesus, God's Son (John 1:29, 34), open the seals on a scroll one by one. Six are already open (Revelation 6). Now the Lamb opens the seventh, the last one, and friend, I'm leaning in SO close.

cards.question: The Lamb opens the seventh seal. What fills heaven?

answers.text: Silence for about half an hour
A new song before the throne
A sound like a mighty wind

cards.text: About half an hour of quiet in heaven, and I shared a drawer with dead batteries that argued NONSTOP, so I can't even PICTURE it. Then John sees the seven angels who stand before God, and they're given seven trumpets.
Then another angel with a golden censer comes and stands at the altar. He's given MUCH incense to offer, and friend, if anybody handed me that much, my mustache would be asking for a cart.

cards.question: The angel with the golden censer is given much incense to offer on the golden altar before the throne. What does he offer along with it?

answers.text: The prayers of all the saints
The crowns of all the elders
The palm branches of the crowd

cards.question: True or false: from the angel's hand, the smoke of the incense and the prayers of the saints fade away before they ever reach God.

cards.text: The prayers of the saints rise up before God. Then the angel fills the censer with fire from the altar, and my eyebrows just climbed halfway up my chef's hat.

cards.question: The angel's censer is full of fire from the altar. What does he do with it?
True or false: when the angel hurls the censer to the earth, there are peals of thunder, rumblings, flashes of lightning and an earthquake.

cards.text: Now the seven angels with the seven trumpets get ready to sound them, and I'm holding my breath like it's the last ten seconds on the oven timer. Then the first angel sounds his trumpet.

cards.question: The first angel sounds his trumpet. What is hurled down upon the earth?

answers.text: Hail and fire mixed with blood

cards.question: When the first trumpet sounds, a third of the earth is ___ up.
True or false: the first trumpet burns up all the green grass.

cards.text: The second angel sounds his trumpet. Something like a great mountain burning with fire is thrown into the sea, and a third of the sea turns to blood.

cards.question: A third of the sea has turned to blood. What happens to the ships on it?

answers.text: A third of them are destroyed
All of them turn back to port

cards.question: True or false: with the second trumpet, every living creature in the sea survives.

cards.text: The third angel sounds his trumpet, and a great star burning like a torch falls from heaven. It lands on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water.
That star has a name: Wormwood. A third of the waters turn bitter like wormwood oil.

cards.question: True or false: when a third of the waters turn bitter, no one is harmed by them.

cards.text: The fourth angel sounds his trumpet, and a third of the sun and moon and stars are struck. Friend, I light my stars one cookie box at a time, so this one hits me RIGHT in the apron.

cards.question: A third of the sun and moon and stars are struck. What happens?

answers.text: A third of day and night go dark
The sun stands still in the sky
The sky rolls up like a scroll

cards.text: Four trumpets down. Then John hears an eagle flying overhead, calling in a loud voice and crying woe three times on those who dwell on the earth.

cards.question: The eagle cries woe to those who dwell on the earth. What is it warning about?

answers.text: The trumpets of the last three angels
A storm about to hit the seas
A famine coming upon the land

cards.text: When an eagle yells woe three times, friend, I do NOT need to hear it a fourth. Three trumpets still to go, and this story's not done, so keep that apron on.
